transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alice Martin (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Chen Wu (Product), Maya Singh (HarborPay CTO), Liam O'Connor (Lead Eng), Sofia Reyes (Platform), Noah Patel (PM)

Summary:
Quick hosted API sandbox orientation focused on chat / text generation basics: streaming behavior, most-used params, retry/backoff patterns, and a short tour of the Console Optimize suggestions. Customer emphasized low-latency for chat support flows and strict data residency / VPC needs for pilot. Agreed next steps for sandbox access, param presets, and VPC details.

Topics covered:
- Hosted API quickstart + sandbox access
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Key params: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences, stream chunk sizing
- Retry and idempotency guidance, exponential backoff and jitter
- Console: request tracing and cost breakdown, Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization
- Pilot success metrics and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alice Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alice from Redwood — i do the AE work. Uh quick who we have on from HarborPay?
[00:00:06] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here. CTO. Liam, Sofia and Noah are on too. Good to meet you.
[00:00:10] Liam O'Connor: Hi all.
[00:00:12] Alice Martin: Great. Devon from our infra team will do the demo and run through the console after the walkthrough.
[00:00:18] Devon Park: Hey all, Devon. I'll share my screen in a sec. We're going to do a short live sandbox run: a chat gen request, show streaming chunks, then show how you tune params and what happens with retries.
[00:00:29] Sofia Reyes: Quick note — HarborPay needs low latency for live chat support, ideally 200-300ms token pacing. Also we have to route traffic through our VPC peering.
[00:00:37] Devon Park: Totally makes sense, thanks. We'll touch on routing and the private options briefly. For the sandbox we'll be on hosted but you can pin a private model later.

[00:01:05] Devon Park: Alright i'm showing the console — here's a sandbox key, quickstart curl snippet. This is the conversation API endpoint, you can use stream=true to get event-stream style chunks.
[00:01:20] Devon Park: I'm going to run a sample prompt for a support assistant. Watch the stream output — you'll see tokens come in as partials and then a final completion.
[00:01:35] [streaming chunks noise, partial transcripts sometimes split]
[00:01:40] Devon Park: (typing) call out: sometimes the transcript shows like a dash or weird capitalization because of ASR, ignore that.
[00:01:46] Liam O'Connor: The stream looks clean. How do you handle mid-response failures?
[00:01:50] Devon Park: Good question. We recommend client side idempotency keys for request-level retries if you resubmit, and server-side we persist the KV cache for the session so small reconnects can resume from cache. The simple pattern is: if you get a network timeout, retry with exponential backoff and the same conversation id; if you get a 4xx permanent error don't retry.
[00:02:10] Maya Singh: Can you show the code snippet for that?
[00:02:13] Devon Park: Sure yeah. (shares code) Here is the curl plus SDK; note we include a header x-idempotency-key and we also show a sequence token for continuations.
[00:02:28] Noah Patel: What's your recommended backoff schedule?
[00:02:31] Devon Park: We usually do base 300ms, then *exponential* multiply by 2 with full jitter, cap at roughly 5 to 10 seconds, try up to 3 retries for transient network errors. For server throttling (429) we honor Retry-After and implement a longer backoff.
[00:02:45] [00:03:00] Chen Wu: Another note: for streaming UX, small chunk sizes help perceived latency; large chunks trade off throughput and cost.
[00:03:10] Liam O'Connor: Do you batch tokens across requests?
[00:03:13] Devon Park: On the hosted path we do continuous batching within the runtime: short latency-aware windows group nearby requests to improve GPU utilization. Console Optimize will show how batching affects unit cost and latency in your workload.
[00:03:25] Maya Singh: We have a concern with hallucination in support replies — any guardrails?
[00:03:29] Chen Wu: You can use structured output rules, tool-calling patterns, and higher top-p/low temperature for deterministic answers. Also run evals with Redwood Optimize: you can upload prompt sets and get regression alerts.
[00:03:44] Sofia Reyes: Is that Optimize feature available on the sandbox?
[00:03:47] Alice Martin: The sandbox has a lightweight Optimize preview; full analytics and longer retention are enterprise add-ons but we'll include a trial for the pilot.
[00:03:55] [00:04:20] Devon Park: Now I'm tweaking params live — setting temperature 0.2, max_tokens 120, and adding a stop sequence — you can see shorter, more deterministic outputs.
[00:04:34] Liam O'Connor: If we lower temperature, what impact on token usage?
[00:04:38] Devon Park: Not much direct impact on token count per se, it changes the distribution of tokens generated but usually stable; you control max_tokens to bound cost. We can show predictive cost in the Console during the run.
[00:04:52] Maya Singh: latency vs cost question — if you need 200ms latency, do you recommend Dedicated?
[00:04:57] Devon Park: For strict sub-200ms tail latency at scale, Dedicated with pinned GPU pools is best. Hosted can hit 200-300ms for many small requests and we provide burst capacity. Also routing to the nearest region reduces network RTT.
[00:05:14] Sofia Reyes: And private deployment options?
[00:05:16] Alice Martin: Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control over data egress and residency, plus KMS integrations. For HarborPay pilot, many customers start hosted sandbox, then move to Dedicated or Private for production.
[00:05:28] [00:05:50] Devon Park: Back to retries — i'm going to simulate a transient failure. (simulates) Client sees a connection drop; we retry with same conversation id, SDK replays minimal delta and requests missing tokens.
[00:06:05] Liam O'Connor: What about duplicate completions if retry goes through twice?
[00:06:08] Devon Park: Use idempotency keys. The server checks the key and returns the same completion if the original succeeded. For streaming, the client should dedupe partials on the idempotency/stream id.
[00:06:22] Maya Singh: Any limits on idempotency keys lifespan?
[00:06:25] Devon Park: We keep them for a short window, usually a few minutes for safety — long-running jobs can use a persistent conversation id pattern. We'll share exact TTLs in the security doc.
[00:06:38] [00:07:10] Chen Wu: Quick Console tour: request trace view shows per-call latency, token counts broken down by prompt vs completion, and cost estimated. Optimize gives model/quantization suggestions by workload, and recommends batch windows for throughput.
[00:07:29] Devon Park: You'll also see per-token cost by model variant; if you select a quantized variant from the catalog we show expected cost and latency delta.
[00:07:40] Sofia Reyes: For PCI scoped data — do you store the transcripts?
[00:07:43] Alice Martin: By default, hosted kept ephemeral logs for a short retention, but for PCI you can opt out: disable logs, or use Private with customer-managed retention and KMS. We'll share our SOC2 docs and the PCI guidance.
[00:07:57] Maya Singh: That's important. Ok.
[00:08:05] [00:08:30] Devon Park: Switching to a quick latency demo: sending 50 small prompts in parallel to show tail percentiles. Console displays P50/P95/P99 and you can drill into traces to see where time is spent (network, queuing, token generation).
[00:08:50] Liam O'Connor: Do you provide SDK-level circuit breaker patterns?
[00:08:53] Devon Park: We provide examples and the SDK has basic retry helpers; for heavier patterns you should implement circuit breakers in your service layer.
[00:09:05] Noah Patel: On billing — how granular is token billing for streamed partials?
[00:09:09] Chen Wu: Billing is per-token consumed; streaming doesn't change cost accounting — you pay for tokens generated. Console shows estimated token cost in real time.
[00:09:21] [00:09:40] Maya Singh: Anything about conversation caching?
[00:09:43] Devon Park: We offer prefix caching and KV cache for long-lived sessions which reduces compute for repeated context. Also shows as cost savings in Optimize.
[00:09:54] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot we want 2k conversations per hour, avg 50 tokens response. Can you ballpark cost?
[00:09:59] Chen Wu: We'll run a quick calc after; i'll include a conservative estimate in the follow-up.
[00:10:10] [00:10:40] Alice Martin: Quick qualifying Qs — what are your timeline and success criteria for pilot?
[00:10:45] Maya Singh: We want a two-week pilot starting late october, success is 95% reduction in avg resolution time on support tickets and P95 latency under 400ms.
[00:10:56] Alice Martin: Great, that's actionable. We'll target those numbers and show config to chase them.
[00:11:05] [00:11:30] Devon Park: A few gotchas: streaming chunk sizes — if you set token_batch_size too high you'll see bigger chunks and perceived latency. Also mixing tool-calls and streaming can require buffering until structured tool response is ready.
[00:11:47] Liam O'Connor: Do you have sample retries built into the JS SDK?
[00:11:50] Devon Park: Yes, examples in the SDK repo. We'll paste links.
[00:12:05] [00:12:30] Chen Wu: For security review we have SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integration. We can do a security deep dive with our compliance team if you want.
[00:12:41] Maya Singh: We'll need SOC2 + encryption at rest details.
[00:12:46] Alice Martin: We'll include SOC2 and encryption docs in the follow-up bundle.
[00:12:52] [00:13:20] Devon Park: One more live thing: i'm going to trigger a 429 by throttling the sandbox to show Retry-After handling. You can see the client backs off and then resumes.
[00:13:36] Noah Patel: Nice. Is there a console alert for throttling?
[00:13:39] Devon Park: Yes, Console shows recent 429s and suggests burst configs and quota increases.
[00:13:48] [00:14:10] Chen Wu: Also Optimize will tell you if your request patterns are inefficient and point to model/quantization swaps.
[00:14:20] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot, we want a simple fallback if the model is unavailable — like a canned response.
[00:14:25] Devon Park: Common pattern: have a fallback route to a lower-cost, smaller model or a static FAQ response. Redwood supports routing policies to failover to a compatible variant.
[00:14:37] Maya Singh: Great.
[00:14:40] [00:15:00] Alice Martin: Time check — we've got about 30 minutes left. Any other must-cover items?
[00:15:06] Sofia Reyes: Network config and peering steps — can you outline?
[00:15:10] Alice Martin: Sure — we have a short VPC peering checklist and shared ip ranges doc; Devon will follow up with specifics for HarborPay.
[00:15:21] Devon Park: I'll attach the checklist. Also note for private deployments there's extra lead time for on-prem approvals.
[00:15:30] [00:15:55] Devon Park: Quick demo wrap: here's an example of reducing tokens using system prompts + truncation, and the Console chart shows estimated cost dropping.
[00:16:06] Liam O'Connor: How do you recommend testing hallucination regression?
[00:16:10] Chen Wu: Upload reference prompts to Optimize, run A/B across model variants and get diffs; Optimize will flag regressions against a golden set.
[00:16:20] Maya Singh: Ok that would help.
[00:16:26] [00:16:45] Noah Patel: Anything else on SLA?
[00:16:48] Alice Martin: Hosted has uptime commitments and we offer SLA-backed Dedicated for higher guarantees; we'll include SLA tiers in the docs.
[00:16:58] [00:17:20] Devon Park: Last live note: when streaming into browsers, consider server-sent events or websockets and make sure your client can gracefully reconnect and dedupe.
[00:17:32] Liam O'Connor: Perfect.
[00:17:40] [00:18:10] Alice Martin: Ok let's recap next steps. We'll spin up sandbox keys for HarborPay, Devon will share param presets and retry playbook, Chen will include a cost estimate, and i'll include security/compliance bundle. Sofia will share VPC details.
[00:18:32] Maya Singh: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[00:18:36] Alice Martin: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a single email that bundles everything and propose kickoff date for the pilot.
[00:18:45] [crosstalk, brief goodbyes]
